title: Palettized KV shard coordinator for heterogeneous GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: As we roll out heterogeneous GPU clusters (A100 + H100 + consumer-grade nodes) continuous batching and KV cache usage become non-uniform. Hot token prefixes create skewed per-GPU memory pressure and cause pipeline stalls or suboptimal spilling. Goal: Introduce a coordinator that assigns 'palettes' (compact contiguous KV slice groups) to GPUs and dynamically remaps palettes at runtime based on token hotness, sequence-length distribution, and pipeline/tensor-parallel placement. This should reduce cross-GPU KV churn, avoid large reallocations during canary rollouts, and keep end-to-end p99 latency within SLOs while improving steady-state throughput and memory utilization.
design_decisions: Use 'palettes' (fixed-size contiguous slice groups) instead of microshards to reduce metadata overhead and cache thrash
Coordinator lives in the serving runtime control plane (per-node) with lightweight cross-node gossip for global cold/hot signals
Allocate palettes with affinity to tensor-parallel placement: prefer palettes that align with model shard ownership to minimize KV transfer across PCIe/NIC
Support asynchronous palette remapping during low-latency windows to avoid stalls; immediate remap only for severe OOM conditions
Spill strategy: prefer local host RAM spill for warm palettes and remote peer spill only when host memory exceeded; avoid spilling to disk for short-lived bursts
Telemetry: track palette hotness, remap frequency, cross-gpu transfer bytes, and end-to-end token latency to drive heuristics
implementation_notes: Coordinator component: go service inside runtime daemon with gRPC debug endpoint and /metrics
New data-structures: PaletteDescriptor {palette_id, start_slice, num_slices, owner_gpu, last_access_ts, hot_score} (serialized flatbuffer)
API changes: runtime Config includes palette_size, max_palettes_per_gpu, remap_threshold_ms, hot_score_half_life
KV placement algorithm: combine LRU-ish hot_score with sequence-length weighted sampling to pick candidate palettes for remap
Integration with continuous batching: when building a batch, the scheduler should attempt to co-locate requests touching same palette to enable local KV reuse
Fallback compatibility: expose 'palette-agnostic' mode for dedicated clusters that want exact legacy semantics
Bench harness: synthetic token streams with Zipfian prefix distribution and production trace replay (see benchmark/run-palettized.sh)
PRs: draft PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342 contains data-structures and simple coordinator; next PR will add remap heuristics and telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature gate off in runtime-1.20-nightly, unit tests + bench harness validated
Phase 1: Canary on non-critical cluster (small heterogeneous pool) with feature enabled, 1% traffic, monitor cross-gpu bytes and p99 latency for 48h
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% in region, enable remap only during low-util windows; record remap frequency and abort if remaps > 10/hour/gpu
Phase 3: Enable aggressive remap heuristics and local spill fallback in dedicated clusters, 72h observation
Rollback: feature flag to disable coordinator, revert placement to legacy slab assignment; save snapshots of palette tables for debugging
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency impact <= +3% vs baseline under mixed-length workload in 95th percentile tests
Average GPU memory utilization variance across nodes reduced by at least 18% for heterogeneous pools in bench snapshots
No increase in observed OOM events during 7-day canary on dedicated cluster
Telemetry is emitted for palette remaps, hot_score, cross_gpu_transfer_bytes, and integrated into Console dashboard (route: /palettes/runtime-1.20)
Documentation: design doc published in Confluence (link), runtime config docs updated, and an operator runbook for safe rollback
